target_customer: Mobile app engineering and QA teams (customers include Duolingo, Lyft, Wayfair, Flo Health)
problem: Mobile end to end tests are slow to write and maintain. MobileBoost's AI agent turns plain language specs into test code, runs them on devices and repairs them when the app changes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (G2 lists a Standard plan at $799 per month)
product_category: AI mobile app test automation (GPT Driver)

founders.name: Christian Schiller
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Oct 2021 (Kitchenful coverage): spent four years as VP of Product at HelloFresh; the company was Kitchenful at that time.

founders.name: Christian Hartung
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Oct 2021: formerly at Rocket Internet.

competitors.name: Lollipop
competitors.what: New online grocery and recipe-based shopping player named as competition for Kitchenful

competitors.name: Plateup
competitors.what: App that converts recipes into grocery lists

technical_complexity.rationale: Kitchenful needed recipe personalization and grocery ordering integrations. The later AI testing product needs device farms and UI models, harder than the original.

defensibility.rationale: Meal planning and grocery concierge had little defensibility. Later testing product competes with mobile.dev Maestro, Waldo and others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company left the meal planning market through a pivot rather than being copied or bought; no incumbent action was found.

market_need_then: Kitchenful targeted time poor consumers wanting cheap meal plans with automatic grocery orders. For the later testing product, Duolingo reported a 70% cut in manual regression testing.

branding.domain_note: Uses mobileboost.io; the YC listing points to a /yc landing page.
branding.brand_signature: Product brand GPT Driver; MobileBoost is the company name

rebrands.why: Company changed from consumer meal planning to AI mobile test automation; the rebrand is stated by Seedtable only and the date is not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post for GPT Driver (YC S21); no further community evidence found

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name and a product brand that competes for attention; the pre-pivot Kitchenful brand received TechCrunch coverage but was dropped.

pivots.from: Kitchenful, meal planning with grocery concierge in Berlin
pivots.to: GPT Driver, AI mobile app test automation
pivots.why: Not stated in sources. A commenter on the Launch HN thread says the first GPT Driver version launched in April 2023.

outcome_analysis: The company went through YC in Summer 2021 as Kitchenful, raised about $1.9M in October 2021, then pivoted into AI mobile test automation, with GPT Driver first shipped around April 2023. It now lists customers such as Duolingo, Lyft and Wayfair. No announced round after 2021 was found, so the pivot succeeded commercially on customer evidence while funding remains unverified.
notes: The Kitchenful to MobileBoost link rests on Seedtable plus matching founder names (Schiller, Hartung) between the YC page and TechCrunch. The mobileboost.io fetch was rate limited and later returned only a title. Startbase reports the seed as 1.6M euros, same round. The 1M pre-seed amount comes from a search summary of the TechCrunch article, not the opened text, and its date is not stated. CB Insights lists 0.5M convertible note and other aggregators list 2M to 3M totals; conflicting. The 8M Driver seed in October 2024 is a different company. Competitors listed are for the original Kitchenful business as of founding; later testing rivals include Maestro/Robin, Waldo and mabl per the Launch HN thread, not as of founding.
